hints.title: Bitwise Disjoint Property
hints.text: A subarray is nice if every pair of elements has bitwise and equal to zero, which means no two numbers share any set bit.

hints.title: Running Bitwise Disjunction
hints.text: Maintain the bitwise or of all numbers currently in the window. When considering nums[right], check if it shares set bits with the running bitwise or.

hints.title: Sliding Window Shrinking
hints.text: While nums[right] & current_or does not equal 0, remove nums[left] from the window by xor-ing it out and increment left.

hints.title: Sliding Window Bitwise OR Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def longestNiceSubarray(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        cur_or = 0
        left = 0
        max_len = 0
        for right in range(len(nums)):
            while (cur_or & nums[right]) != 0:
                cur_or ^= nums[left]
                left += 1
            cur_or |= nums[right]
            max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)
        return max_len
```

complexity.notes: Each element is added and removed from the bitwise mask at most once (window size <= 30).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs of elements across all subarrays takes O(n^3) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bitwise accumulation maintains window state in a single 32-bit integer.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Uses bitwise OR accumulation with sliding window to achieve linear time complexity.
